articles.content:
November 23, 2026

An open-source runtime that helps operators protect running Linux systems without needing to wait for the patch or restarts

OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches. In acontrolled test⁠(opens in a new window), a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart.

We’re inviting developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators across the industry to help develop the project further. The project brings together OpenAI’s frontier AI, security and infrastructure research and Cisco’s infrastructure and security expertise to help protect the systems people rely on every day.

Testing and deploying a patch can still take days or weeks. Protecting a service in the meantime can be challenging because an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same Linux operation. Blocking that operation entirely could take the service offline.

Shirudo (Japanese for “shield”) is designed to help security teams navigate this tradeoff. Teams can test whether a temporary safeguard, called a shield, blocks the behavior that exposes a vulnerability while allowing legitimate requests through. Once an operator approves the shield, it can be deployed while the service continues running.

Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system. This makes it possible to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted security protections to running systems.

How the guardian agent observes and protects a running system with eBPF.

OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo around four core capabilities:

Live protection:eBPF shields can block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system. Security teams can monitor how a proposed shield would affect applications before enforcing it.

Defense at machine speed:OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo to give agents programmable controls to investigate vulnerabilities, develop targeted shields, and validate their effectiveness against exploits and real workloads. Security teams control what gets deployed.

Trusted deployment:Shields are cryptographically signed and verified before loading. Linux's eBPF verifier checks eBPF programs against its safety rules, while kernel security controls restrict unauthorized changes.

Hardware-backed verification:Shirudo uses a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) to support a verifiable record of protections being loaded or removed. Operators can use this evidence to check whether systems meet their security requirements.

TheShirudo technical walkthrough⁠(opens in a new window)from the Linux Plumbers Conference shows how toapply a shield and verify it on the target host⁠(opens in a new window). The Java4Shell vulnerability is another example illustrating how a targeted shield can protect a running application while a permanent patch is being prepared. Using OpenAI's Codex, the team generated a shield that added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder and attached it directly to a running Elasticsearch process. When attempting to exploit the vulnerability, the shield rejected the malicious input, blocking the attack while Elasticsearch continued running. You can read morehere⁠(opens in a new window).

Shirudo is a first step toward infrastructure that can adapt to emerging threats while remaining reliable. We want to strengthen the operating system foundations needed to deploy these protections at scale, including hardening the kernel and core services, limiting workload permissions, and making updates and recovery safer.

Our long-term goal is to enable defenders and AI agents to quickly identify affected systems, validate protections, and deploy eBPF shields that block exploits without disrupting workloads. Applications should run with only the permissions they need, governed by policies that are automatically generated and maintained.

We will combine frontier AI with security and infrastructure research to discover vulnerabilities and test defenses against realistic attacks. We aim to make it easier for operators to detect and contain compromises, prevent attackers from moving across systems, and restore services to a verified, known-good state. Hardware-backed attestation and independent network controls provide additional assurance even if individual systems are compromised.

OpenAI and Cisco are open-sourcingShirudo⁠(opens in a new window)so developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators can inspect the code, test protections, and contribute to its development. Shirudo is licensed under BSD 2-Clause, with its BPF programs dual-licensed under BSD and GPL.

Our goal is to make tested shields available alongside vulnerability disclosures, giving operators a way to evaluate and deploy temporary protections while preparing permanent patches.

Try Shirudo:Follow theVM quickstart⁠(opens in a new window)to sign, load, and verify a test protection.

Get hands-on:Explore Shirudo throughIsovalent's self-guided lab⁠(opens in a new window).

Join the technical deep dive:Register for theDecember 15 webinar⁠(opens in a new window).

We’re building Shirudo in the open with the people who build, run, and secure Linux systems. We welcome contributions to the runtime, new shields, and improvements to Linux and eBPF. If you'd like to get involved, take a look at thecode on GitHub⁠(opens in a new window), read thedocs⁠(opens in a new window), andlet us know what you find⁠(opens in a new window).

Linux의 eBPF를 활용해 취약한 실행 경로를 선택적으로 차단하며, 운영자는 정상 요청에 미치는 영향을 확인하고 승인한 뒤 재시작 없이 임시 보호 장치를 적용할 수 있다. 통제된 시험에서는 Codex가 생성한 보호 장치가 실행 중인 Elasticsearch 서비스에 대한 Java4Shell 공격 시도를 차단했다고 보고했다. 패치 적용 전 노출 시간을 줄이는 접근이지만, 제시된 시험만으로 다양한 운영 환경에서의 효과를 일반화하기는 어렵다.

articles.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship for GitHub Pull Request Review and Fixes
articles.content: Anthropic just released Claude Ship. Claude Ship is a set of Anthropic agents that takes GitHub pull requests from review to approval. It bundles 3 agents: Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals. Your GitHub branch rules still decide what merges. TL;DR Size: 3 agents with a local /ship command. Runs on: Anthropic’s cloud for Code Review and PR Steward. /ship runs in the Claude Code CLI locally. Performance: Most Code Reviews finish in 6 to 10 minutes, about 3x faster than the research preview. Best: Claude Code team merged PRs more than doubled from June to September (self-reported). What is Claude Ship? Per the Claude Ship docs, each agent owns 1 step: Code Review looks for logic errors, security vulnerabilities and broken edge cases. Findings land as inline comments, ranked by severity. PR Steward works on failing checks, merge conflicts and review comments. It pushes commits with its fixes. Claude Approvals checks each PR against an approval policy your team writes. Code Review is generally available. The other 2 are in public beta. How does Claude Ship work on a pull request? Code Review finds problems. PR Steward pushes fixes, and a fix can start another review. Claude Approvals then applies your policy. The merge follows your GitHub branch rules. PR Steward is designed not to approve or merge. After each push, it comments on its changes and how to undo them. Developers steer it with @claude and stop it with @claude stop. Claude Approvals reads a policy file at .claude/approvals.yml. Anthropic calls it a smarter CODEOWNERS file. A rule can require 2 people on billing code and 1 on test fixtures. Rules can read PR facts and classifier answers, but not CI results. What does /ship do for developers? Developers run /ship in Claude Code. It commits, pushes and opens the PR. Claude reviews it, then ‘watches’ feedback and failing checks. You merge yourself. Requirements are Claude Code v2.1.330 or later, GitHub CLI 2.63 or later, and git 2.38 or later. A watch ends after 7 days, or on merge or close. /steward skips the review on an open PR. When Claude acts alone, Claude Code blocks merge, approve, auto-merge and force-push commands. Still, a watch uses your own gh and git sign-ins. Claude Ship benchmarks: what has Anthropic reported? Anthropic has published no public benchmark. It shares internal results from its launch post and engineering blog: Merged PRs on the Claude Code team more than doubled from June to September. The share of reverted changes fell by more than 40% over the same period. Internal PRs with substantive review comments rose from 16% to 54%. PRs passing after 1 review-and-fix round rose from 65% to 78%. Mean reviews needed to pass fell from 2.08 to 1.32. These numbers are self-reported by Anthropic. No precision or recall is reported. &&& How does Claude Ship compare with Copilot, Bugbot and CodeRabbit? Claude Ship pricing, deployment and availability Claude Ship is for Claude Team and Enterprise plans on GitHub. Owners enable agents per repository, ideally 1 at a time. Billing runs on tokens through usage credits, separate from plan usage. Code Review costs scale with PR count, size, review level and frequency. Admins can set spend limits. PR Steward has none until an Owner sets one. Approvals has no base charge. Classifier runs and the reviews a policy requests are billed, even in observe mode. Running /ship counts as regular Claude Code usage. Eligible Enterprise organizations can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits by January 15, 2027. Credits expire 30 days after claiming, per the credit terms. Key Takeaways Claude Ship bundles 3 GitHub agents: Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals. Code Review is GA; PR Steward and Approvals are in public beta. Approval rules live in .claude/approvals.yml; start in observe mode. Anthropic reports over 2x merged PRs and over 40% fewer reverts (self-reported). Token billing, Team and Enterprise only, no ZDR, HIPAA or CMEK. articles.title: Z AI Releases GLM-5.4: A 750B Loop Transformer That Runs 28 Layers Twice
articles.content: Z.ai has released GLM-5.4, its first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer architecture. The GLM-5.4 Loop Transformer runs 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model for 2 iterations. Z.ai says the model reaches intelligence comparable to 2T-3T parameter models. For developers, the pitch is ‘Generalized Coding’: code as the tool for video, games, 3D shaders and CAD. TL;DR Size: 750B-scale base. Active parameters not disclosed. Context window not officially listed (the blog discusses deployment at 1M context). Runs on: Z.ai-hosted only for now (GLM Coding Plan, ZCode, Z.ai Chat). Self-hosting hardware not disclosed until weights ship. Performance: No flagship benchmark table yet. Z.ai claims parity with 2T-3T parameter models. Best: +11.3 points on AIME25 (19.17 to 30.42) in Z.ai’s 30B looped ablation. Worst: +3.3 points on IFBench (50.20 to 53.47), the smallest gain. Z.ai also flags “marathon thinking” loops. What is GLM-5.4? GLM-5.4 is a 750B-scale Loop Transformer from Z.ai that runs shared layers twice per pass. It ships first inside Z.ai’s own products: the GLM Coding Plan, the ZCode desktop app and Z.ai Chat. Z.ai did not pre-train a looped model from scratch. It adapted the pre-trained GLM-5 base through continued training. The technical post states that looped models trained from scratch still trail unshared models at equal compute. Adapting an existing base raises the ceiling with a relatively small compute overhead. How does the Loop Transformer work? In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In GLM-5.4, a group of 28 weight-shared layers runs for 2 iterations. Z.ai made 3 changes to keep this practical at 750B scale. Gated progressive updates Overwriting hidden states across loops made activation norms blow up. GLM-5.4 adds independent per-token gates for each iteration. The first pass writes small updates and builds global context. The second pass opens the gates to refine the output. On harder tokens, the first pass writes more aggressively. Hybrid KV cache A naive design keeps a full KV cache for every loop. GLM-5.4’s second loop reuses the sparse KV selected in pass 1. It keeps its own new KV only inside a local sliding window. So the extra loop costs 1 sliding window of KV cache, not a full context cache. Z.ai says this keeps the cost increase over GLM-5.3 under control at 1M context. Sparse attention index reuse The second loop reuses the indices from the first loop’s indexer. That adds zero indexing overhead. Z.ai reports near-identical results versus recomputing indices on every pass. &&&& How does GLM-5.4 perform on benchmarks? Z.ai has not published benchmark scores for the 750B GLM-5.4 model. A Z.ai team member said scores will come later, per DataCamp. The evidence in the blog is an iso-parameter ablation on a 30B model. It shares the 750B base’s architecture. The looped version used about 10% more total training compute. Scores were measured after 200K long-context SFT with thinking mode on. Benchmark (30B ablation)Baseline+ LoopGainAvg. output length changeAIME2519.1730.42+11.3-635 tokens (-2%)GPQA-Diamond47.5856.26+8.7-2,473 tokens (-11.7%)AA-LCR40.3347.67+7.3-539 tokens (-9.7%)MMLU-Pro71.6575.05+3.4-863 tokens (-14.9%)IFBench50.2053.47+3.3-763 tokens (-13.0%) Source: Z.ai GLM-5.4 blog. Self-reported, 30B model, not the 750B flagship. Two patterns stand out. The largest gains come in math, science reasoning and long context. Output length also falls on most tasks. MMLU-Pro answers got 14.9% shorter and GPQA-Diamond answers 11.7% shorter. Z.ai says part of the reasoning moves into the loop’s implicit depth. AIME25 is the exception: output length dropped only 2%. Z.ai validated the design on 1B, 4B, 30B and 750B bases. The ‘2T-3T parameter’ claim has no flagship table behind it yet. What can GLM-5.4 do beyond traditional coding? Z.ai calls this direction Generalized Coding. It credits gains in both coding and vision. The technical sections shows four demos: Video: a self-narrated music video called “Hello World”. Engineering: a 6-axis robotic arm built through CAD modeling in FreeCAD. Games: a complete game with movement, physics, maps, combat and art assets. 3D: an interactive bird-watching scene built with math geometry and custom GLSL shaders. These are vendor demos, not benchmarks. How fast is GLM-5.4 and where can developers use it? Z.ai reports up to 200 tokens/s off-peak and 70-80 tokens/s at peak load. It fused core kernels to cut intermediate memory traffic. Access today runs through the GLM Coding Plan, ZCode and Z.ai Chat. ZCode is Z.ai’s desktop agent harness for GLM-5.4. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux (Beta). The Coding Plan lists Lite at $12.6/month, Pro at $56 and Max at $117.6. Z.ai says prices may change. How does GLM-5.4 compare with other open frontier models? articles.title: Meta TLX Brings Warp-Group GPU Control to Triton on Hopper, Blackwell, AMD
articles.content: Meta has published a detailed report on TLX (Triton Low-Level Extensions). It is the GPU compiler extension behind Meta’s production ML kernels. Meta TLX is a Triton extension that exposes warp groups, barriers, TMA and clusters to Python kernels. It targets NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell plus AMD MI300 and MI350-series GPUs. For kernel engineers, the message is CUDA-level control without leaving Triton. TL;DR What it is: an extension to Triton, not a new language. A Blackwell GEMM takes roughly 200 lines of Python-level Triton. Runs on: NVIDIA Hopper (H100) and Blackwell (B200, GB200), AMD MI300 and MI350-series. MIT-licensed. Performance: within -0.9% to +3.7% of cuBLAS on 6 H100 FP16 GEMM shapes (PyTorch). Best: a 4x speedup on an H100 linear compression kernel for ads inference (Meta). Worst: dense LLM-style attention forward reaches about 87% of FlashAttention-4 on B200 (PyTorch). Bottom line: Best: hand-tuned performance from short Triton code. Worst: all numbers are self-reported, with no independent benchmarks yet. What is TLX and what problem does it solve? Triton programs GPUs at the block level. CUDA programs them at the thread level. Modern GPUs need something in between. Hopper introduced warp specialization and the Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA). Blackwell added tensor memory (TMEM), cluster execution and paired-CTA execution. Meta says CUDA could express these patterns, but only with large amounts of architecture-specific code. TLX fills that gap with a model the research team calls MIMW (Multi-Instruction, Multi-Warp). The warp group becomes the basic unit of orchestration. Triton still defines what runs. TLX defines how it is orchestrated. Engineers write ordinary Triton and add TLX calls only where control matters. How does TLX work? TLX adds 5 extension areas on top of Triton: Warp-group orchestration: warp groups get roles such as producer, consumer and epilogue. Synchronization: warp groups sync through hardware mbarriers. Thread-level sync stays with the compiler. Memory orchestration: direct access to TMA, asynchronous tensor-core ops and TMEM. Cluster execution: multiple CTAs cooperate through distributed shared memory and cluster-wide barriers. Optional layouts: the compiler infers layouts. Programmers override them only for speed. The API reads like Triton. Meta’s Blackwell matmul example uses tlx.local_alloc, tlx.alloc_barriers, tlx.async_task, tlx.async_dot and tlx.barrier_wait. How fast is TLX? Benchmarks All figures below are self-reported by Meta: H100 GEMM: across 6 FP16 shapes, TLX lands between -0.9% and +3.7% of cuBLAS. On 8192x8192x8192 it reaches 577.0 TFLOPS versus 582.3 for cuBLAS (PyTorch). MI350 GEMM: TLX beats rocBLAS by 11.8% to 15.2% on square shapes from 256 to 2048. B200 attention: On production jagged shapes, Meta’s Jagged Flash Attention beats FlashAttention-4 by about 13% forward. Backward runs about 50% faster. On dense LLM-style shapes, forward reaches about 87% of FA4 (PyTorch). Code size: that attention kernel is about 3.2K lines. Meta estimates FA4 at 10K lines of CuTe DSL. The research team adds that TLX trails state-of-the-art attention most on the smallest causal-forward cases. The gap narrows as sequence length grows. && Where is TLX used in production at Meta? Meta’s engineering post lists 3 case studies: Generative Ads Model (GEM) training: 20% to 25% end-to-end MFU on thousands of GPUs. TLX delivered up to 2x forward speedup for Generalized Dot Product Attention. In-Kernel Broadcast Optimization (IKBO): a warp-specialized linear compression kernel hit 4x speedup on H100. FlashAttention under IKBO cut compute-intensive net latency by up to two-thirds. Distributed grouped GEMM: fuses mixture-of-experts matmuls with communication for LLM pretraining on Blackwell. Meta gives no speedup figure. Meta also compared CUTLASS, CuTe DSL and TLX on Blackwell for GEM. It says TLX gave the best productivity-performance balance for most kernels, but shares no numbers. How do developers install and use TLX? TLX lives in Meta’s MIT-licensed Triton fork, facebookexperimental/triton, under third_party/tlx/. It also ships as triton-utlx on PyPI, a plugin for upstream Triton. The PyTorch-Triton 3.7 plugin system loads TLX without forking Triton. AMD has also published a GEMM plus activation guide for CDNA4 with TLX. TLX vs Gluon vs CuTe DSL vs TileLang FeatureMeta TLXGluonCuTe DSLTileLangMaintainerMeta with UC San Diego (paper)Triton projectNVIDIAtile-ai open source projectApproachExtension on top of Triton; warp-group orchestration; layouts optionalLower-level Triton dialect; tensors carry explicit layouts (AMD)Python DSL isomorphic with CuTe C++ (FAQ)Tile-level DSL with layout and pipeline controlHardwareHopper, Blackwell, AMD MI300 and MI350 (Meta)NVIDIA Hopper+ for warp specialization (docs); AMD MI350/MI355 (AMD)NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper, BlackwellCUDA, ROCm, Metal, CPU, Ascend (SourceForge mirror)LicenseMIT (repo)MIT (part of Triton)NVIDIA EULA for CuTe DSL files (license)MIT (mirror)Headline published result-0.9% to +3.7% vs cuBLAS, H100 FP16 GEMMNot disclosedUsed for FlashAttention-4 kernels, ~10K lines per Meta’s estimate (PyTorch)Not disclosedKnown production useMeta ads training, ads inference, LLM pretrainingNot disclosedFlashAttention-4DeepSeek TileKernels (repo) Key Takeaways TLX adds warp-group, barrier, TMA and cluster control to ordinary Triton code. It lands within -0.9% to +3.7% of cuBLAS on H100 FP16 GEMM. Production wins include 4x on an H100 ads kernel and 20% to 25% MFU on GEM. Dense attention forward still trails FA4 at about 87% on B200. It is MIT-licensed and loads into upstream Triton as a plugin. Check out the paper on arXiv, the Meta engineering post and the GitHub repo. articles.summary: Meta가 실제 머신러닝 커널에 사용하는 Triton 확장 TLX의 상세 보고서를 공개했다고 보도됐다. TLX는 Python 기반 Triton 커널에서 워프 그룹, 배리어, TMA, 클러스터를 제어하도록 하며 NVIDIA Hopper·Blackwell과 AMD MI300·MI350 계열을 대상으로 한다. 일부 H100 행렬곱 시험에서는 cuBLAS 대비 -0.9%~+3.7%의 성능을, 광고 추론용 특정 커널에서는 4배 가속을 보고했다. GPU별 저수준 최적화를 Triton 안에서 수행할 수 있다는 의미가 있지만, 수치는 자체 보고이며 일부 어텐션 작업은 비교 구현보다 느렸다.

articles.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
articles.content: Amazon is acquiring Decart’s AI optimization technology and research team in a reported $7.5 billion deal.
articles.summary: Amazon이 Decart의 AI 최적화 기술과 연구팀을 인수하며 거래 규모는 75억 달러로 보도됐다. 기사 제목은 이를 Amazon의 Trainium 칩 판매 준비와 연결해 소개한다. AI 반도체 사업에 최적화 기술과 연구 인력을 결합하는 움직임이지만, 제공된 자료에는 구체적인 최적화 방식이나 통합 일정, 성능 효과가 제시되지 않았다.

articles.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
articles.content: By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that's already within its ecosystem
articles.summary: Google 검색의 AI Mode가 Drive와 Wallet 데이터를 활용해 더 개인화된 응답을 제공할 수 있게 됐다고 보도됐다. 자료는 Personal Intelligence의 적용 범위를 Drive, Wallet, Gemini 앱으로 확대하는 움직임으로 설명한다. 검색 응답에 Google 생태계 내 사용자 정보를 연결한다는 변화지만, 구체적인 접근 권한 설정과 데이터 처리 조건은 제공된 내용에서 확인되지 않는다.

articles.title: AI 신입사원을 뉴스 데이터 시니어로 키우는 레포, news-data
articles.content: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 AI 에이전트가 뉴스 데이터를 직접 찾고 추출·분석까지 수행하는 하네스 레포 news-data를 소개합니다. 작업마다 배운 것을 회고와 PR로 되돌려 도메인을 모르는 신입사원 같은 에이전트를 시니어로 키우는 과정과 운영하며 부딪힌 한계, 앞으로의 방향을 공유합니다. ​ 발표 대상 코딩 에이전트에게 사내 도메인 업무를 맡겨 보고 싶은 개발자 흩어진 데이터 문서와 도메인 지식을 정리하고 싶은 데이터 엔지니어·분석가 AGENTS.md, 스킬, 규칙으로 에이전트의 작업 방식을 설계해 보고 싶은 분 ​ 목차 1. 왜 만들었나 스키마만으로는 알 수 없는 컬럼의 의미, wiki·GitHub·코드 주석에 흩어진 문서, 담당자 머릿속의 노하우. SQL과 Spark는 잘 쓰지만 우리 조직의 사정은 모르는, 똑똑한 AI 신입사원의 문제 ​ 2. 어떻게 키우나 처음부터 다 모으지 않고 실제 업무를 맡기며, 작업마다 회고를 쓰고 PR로 레포에 되돌리는 작업 루프. 규칙 로드 · 스킬 선택 · 요청·데이터 파악 · 승인 후 실행·검증 · 회고·반영, 요청 한 건이 처리되는 다섯 단계. 그 결과 업무 40건 처리, 이슈부터 회고 PR까지 중앙값 1.6시간, 데이터 분석가 수준의 심층 분석까지 ​ 3. 어디까지 왔나 검토 병목 · 정합성 · 방향성, 키우면서 부딪힌 세 가지 한계. 그리고 계획과 실행을 리모트 데이터 에이전트로 옮기는 다음 단계 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.(관련 포스팅 보기) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립(@devrel_d2)으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.
articles.summary: 네이버가 AI 에이전트의 뉴스 데이터 탐색·추출·분석을 지원하는 하네스 저장소 news-data의 운영 경험을 공개했다. 규칙 로드와 스킬 선택, 요청·데이터 파악, 승인 후 실행·검증, 회고·반영을 연결해 업무에서 얻은 도메인 지식을 PR로 축적한다. 발표에서는 업무 40건을 처리했고 이슈부터 회고 PR까지 걸린 시간의 중앙값이 1.6시간이었다고 보고했다. 사내 데이터 업무에 에이전트를 적응시키는 실무 사례로, 검토 병목과 정합성, 방향성 문제는 남은 한계로 제시됐다.

articles.title: 뇌를 닮은 세컨드 브레인: 토큰 낭비 없는 RAG
articles.content: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ 발표 내용 기존 RAG의 텍스트 덤프 및 토큰 낭비 한계를 극복하고, 최신 인지 메모리 논문 기법을 결합해 지식 자율 진화와 99% 재현율을 달성하는 차세대 AI 메모리 아키텍처를 소개합니다. ​ 발표 대상 RAG의 검색 효율과 답변 품질 개선에 관심 있는 개발자 AI 에이전트의 메모리 관리와 토큰 비용 절감에 관심 있는 개발자 ​ 목차 요청마다 다시 읽히는 토큰 다시 읽는 토큰 가운데 실제로 쓰이는 비율 넣은 4k 토큰 가운데 정답 근거의 비율 목차에서 잘린 규칙을 모델이 열어 보지 않는 문제 쓰지도 않는 토큰이 비싼 이유 크기 × 요청 수로 불어나는 비용 식 늘 넣기, 위치만 두기, 빼 두기: 무엇을 늘 넣어 둘까 Haema(해마)의 구조 층 구조: 기억 저장, 불러오기, 작업 기억, 세션 나누기, 판정 게이트 질문 하나가 지나는 여섯 단계 긴 대화를 위한 세션 롤오버와 기존 compact의 차이 기본값을 바꾸는 판정 게이트 만들고 나서 측정한 결과 대표 실측 넷: 문장 고르기, 중복 제거, 통째로 넣는 RAG와의 비교, 세션 롤오버 통째로 넣는 RAG와 Haema의 재현율·토큰 비교 긴 코딩 과제에서 본 토큰과 기억 시험 다른 장치들: 두 단 목차, 후속 질문 풀어 쓰기, 합치지 않고 쌓기 우리 팀에 적용하기 실험에서 뽑은 여덟 가지 지금 버전이 나오기까지 거친 세 번의 판정 지금 기본으로 쓰는 것과 선택 설정 먼저 측정해 볼 세 가지 비율과 장치를 붙일 수 있는 자리 우리 팀의 RAG와 에이전트에 던져 볼 질문 네 가지 다시 읽히는 토큰에게 '쓰이고 있니?'를 묻기 ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.(관련 포스팅 보기) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립(@devrel_d2)으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.
articles.summary: 네이버가 기존 RAG에서 사용하지 않는 텍스트까지 반복 투입하는 문제를 줄이기 위한 AI 메모리 아키텍처 Haema를 소개했다. 기억 저장·검색·작업 기억·세션 분리·판정 게이트를 결합하고, 긴 대화에서는 세션 롤오버를 활용하는 구조다. 발표 소개는 99% 재현율 달성을 주장하며 전체 텍스트를 넣는 RAG와의 토큰 사용량 및 재현율 비교를 다룬다고 밝혔다. 에이전트의 기억 유지와 비용 절감에 관련된 접근이지만, 제공된 자료에는 평가 데이터와 상세 측정 조건이 없다.

articles.title: Architect Labs Unveils Frostbite, an Interaction Net CPU Designed by AI
articles.content: Architect Labs has introduced Frostbite, an AI-designed CPU with a new instruction set built around interaction nets. The company states that its AI agents designed Frostbite from interaction net theory down to final GDS. In pre-silicon tests, it reports 4.59x the performance per watt of a modern in-order CPU core. TL;DR Size: 1 quad (2×2 tiles) plus 4 L3 nodes takes 0.792 mm² on 7 nm. No parameter count (it is a CPU). Runs on: Pre-silicon only. Final GDS closes at 500 MHz on 7 nm. An FPGA-hosted playground is planned. Performance: 4.59x perf per watt (geomean, 25 workloads) and 8.77x perf per area vs 1 in-order core. Best: 23.12x perf per watt on conv2d. What is Frostbite? Frostbite is a CPU from Architect Labs that executes programs as interaction nets in hardware. Programs are written in Vine, a Rust-like language, and compiled to an IR called Ivy. The chip is a mesh of tiles, each with its own small local memory. The launch post on X states that the AI agents co-designed the ISA and chip architecture given only interaction net theory. How do interaction nets enable parallelism? Interaction nets were introduced by Yves Lafont at POPL 1990. A program is a graph of nodes. Computation rewrites pairs of nodes connected through their ports. Each node has 1 principal port, so active pairs never overlap and can fire in any order. Every value is used exactly once, so there is no shared mutable state to guard. A 5-queens net has 3,183 interactions and a 262-step critical path. About 12 interactions are ready per step. Software runtimes such as HVM2 already run interaction nets on GPUs. Frostbite moves the model into the ISA itself. How is the Frostbite hardware organized? The chip is built from tiles grouped into 2×2 quads. Each tile has front end, engine, memory and system blocks. A runtime domain adds a frame manager, scheduler, work queue and outlet. Its ISA adds wide bundles, hardware loop counters, streams, and ops that take, peek or copy values. Each tile runs its own queued work first. If idle, it takes work from a neighbor. If none is found, it goes inactive to save power. The company says this work stealing emerged during design and was not hand-specified. How did AI agents design the chip? Agents first synthesized papers and built Python models. Their output was a 141-page PDF. It was deleted after the first RTL pass because its estimates were physically unrealistic. The research team then used ASL, an in-house, machine-checkable specification language. ASL is the single source of truth for the ISA, the Arcmodel system model, RTL and verification. The spec translates to Lean, and the project passed 800k lines of Lean. Arcmodel first diverged from RTL by almost 250% in the worst case. An automated fitting pipeline cut that to under 6% worst case and about 1.5% median. Arcmodel simulates the full chip 660x faster than RTL. Across 4 searches and an ablation round, agents tried 58 ideas and kept 37. The design targets 7 nm, timing at 800 MHz in synthesis and 500 MHz in final GDS. It follows Redwood, an edge AI accelerator the company announced in August 2026. How does Frostbite perform on benchmarks? The baseline is ‘TCPU,’ 1 core of a modern dual-issue, in-order superscalar CPU. Architect Labs does not name it, citing legal reasons. 1 Frostbite quad plus 4 L3 nodes occupies 0.792 mm². TCPU occupies 0.895 mm² on the same process. Across 25 workloads, geomean performance per watt is 4.59x. The 10-workload search set scores 6.02x, and the 15-workload held-out set 3.83x. Results range from 23.12x on conv2d to 1.15x on fib. Performance per area averages 8.77x. Fetch, decode and issue fall from 27% of TCPU energy to 6% in a quad. The on-chip network and scheduler take 26% instead. The fft, radixsort and LU kernels follow SPLASH-2, scaled down 64x. & How does Frostbite compare with other approaches? articles.summary: Architect Labs가 상호작용 넷을 하드웨어에서 실행하는 AI 설계 CPU Frostbite를 공개했다고 보도됐다. 프로그램을 그래프로 표현하고 서로 겹치지 않는 노드 쌍의 재작성 연산을 병렬 실행하며, 타일별 로컬 메모리를 갖춘 구조를 채택했다. 회사는 AI 에이전트가 이론부터 최종 GDS까지 설계했으며, 제작 전 25개 워크로드 시험에서 비교 대상 인오더 CPU 코어 대비 전력당 성능 4.59배를 기록했다고 주장했다. 새로운 실행 모델과 AI 기반 칩 설계의 결합이지만, 아직 실리콘 실측 결과는 아니다.

articles.content: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ 발표 내용 개발과 운영 당번을 함께 맡으며 새벽 알림에 깨는 일, 언제까지 사람이 해야 할까요? 원인을 찾는 일부터 직접 조치하는 일까지 AI Agent에게 안심하고 맡길 수 있도록 풀어 간 경험을 공유 드립니다. ​ 발표 대상 개발과 서비스 운영(온콜)을 함께 맡고 있는 개발자·엔지니어 AI Agent에게 조사·조치 같은 실제 운영 업무를 맡기려는 개발자 사내 Agent 도입을 검토하는 팀 ​ 목차 도입 - 어느 조직에나 있는 문제 운영 대상은 늘고, 사람은 준다 온콜이 실제로 하는 일 열한 달의 여정 조사하는 Agent - 1단계 맡기려 했지만, 줄 게 없었다 ① 알림을 한 곳으로 ② 기억과 지식을 준다 응답 형식 케이스 ① 조사하는 Agent 손을 쓰는 Agent - 2단계 넘어야 할 질문 셋 Q1 뭘 할 수 있나 - 능력 Q2 언제 해도 되나 - 판정 Q3 틀리면 어떻게 되나 - 안전망 케이스 ② 무인 조치와 3장 정리 결론 어떻게 도는가 Agent의 진화와 운영 결과 앞으로 Takeaway ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.(관련 포스팅 보기) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립(@devrel_d2)으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

articles.title: AI 로봇이 교정시설 자율 순찰…미국 AITX, 보안 인력 지원·운영비 절감 실증 착수
articles.content:
피지컬 AI(Physical AI) 기반 자율주행 로봇의 활용 범위가 제조·물류 현장을 넘어 교정시설의 보안 순찰 업무로 확대되고 있다.

미국 인공지능(AI) 기반 보안 솔루션 기업 아티피셜 인텔리전스 테크놀로지 솔루션스(Artificial Intelligence Technology Solutions, AITX)는 자회사 로보틱 어시스턴스 디바이시스(Robotic Assistance Devices, RAD)가 교정시설에 자율주행 보안 로봇 ‘로미오(ROAMEO)’의 배치를 완료하고 시설 외곽 순찰을 시작했다고 23일(현지시간) 밝혔다.

지난 11일 발표한 30일간의 개념검증(PoC) 계획에 따른 것으로, 정식 실증 평가에 앞서 현장 배치와 자율 순찰에 돌입한 것이다. 실증은 기존 순찰 차량에 대한 의존도를 낮추고 차량 운영·유지 비용을 절감하는 동시에 교정시설 보안 인력의 업무 수행 범위를 확대할 수 있는지 평가하는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

로미오는 자율주행 기술과 AI 영상 분석, 지능형 상황 감지, 실시간 통신 기능을 결합한 이동형 보안 로봇이다. 시설 외곽을 순찰하면서 의심스러운 활동과 금지 물품의 반입 가능성을 감지하고 관련 정보를 보안관제센터와 시설 관리자에게 전달하도록 설계됐다.

고정형 보안 카메라와 달리 이상 상황이 발생한 지점으로 이동해 보다 가까운 거리에서 현장을 확인하고 보안 인력의 상황 판단을 지원할 수 있다. 특히 RAD의 에이전틱 AI(Agentic AI) 플랫폼인 ‘사라(SARA·Speaking Autonomous Responsive Agent)’를 통해 현장에 있는 사람과 직접 대화하거나 음성 경고를 전달할 수 있다.

사라는 영상과 음성, 센서 데이터를 분석하고 사전에 설정된 운영 목적과 인간의 감독 체계에 따라 상황별 대응을 지원하는 AI 시스템이다.

AITX와 RAD의 창업자이자 최고경영자(CEO) 겸 최고기술책임자(CTO)인 스티브 레인하르츠(Steve Reinharz)는 자율주행 로봇 개발에 그치지 않고 실제 고객 현장에 배치해 운용하는 기술적·사업적 실행 역량이 중요하다고 강조했다.

미국 연방수사국(FBI) 특수요원 출신인 트로이 매캐나(Troy McCanna) RAD 최고보안책임자(CSO) 겸 최고매출책임자(CRO)는 로미오의 현장 접근과 영상 확인, 사라를 통한 의사소통 기능이 교정시설 보안 인력의 상황 판단을 지원하며, 최종 대응에 대한 통제권은 보안 인력이 유지한다고 설명했다.

AITX는 교정시설을 물류센터 등 대규모 시설과 함께 자율 보안 로봇 사업의 새로운 성장 시장으로 보고 있다. 실증 결과에 따라 해당 교정시설 운영기관에 수십 대의 로미오를 추가 공급할 가능성도 열려 있다.

한편, 로미오의 교정시설 배치는 피지컬 AI의 이동·감지 능력과 에이전틱 AI의 상황 분석·대응 기능을 결합한 공공안전 분야의 적용 사례라는 점에서 주목된다. 반복적인 순찰 업무를 로봇이 지원하고 인간은 상황 판단과 최종 대응을 담당하는 협업 모델로, 향후 공항과 항만, 국가 주요 기반시설 등 대규모 보안관리 환경으로의 확장 가능성도 기대된다.
articles.summary: 미국 AITX의 자회사 RAD가 교정시설에 자율 보안 로봇 ROAMEO를 배치하고 외곽 순찰을 시작했다고 밝혔다. 로봇은 자율주행, AI 영상 분석, 상황 감지, 실시간 통신을 결합하며 SARA 플랫폼을 통해 현장 대화와 음성 경고도 지원한다. 30일 개념검증은 순찰 차량 의존도와 운영 비용을 줄이고 보안 인력의 업무 범위를 확대할 수 있는지 평가한다. 최종 대응 통제권은 사람이 유지하며, 비용 절감 효과와 추가 공급 여부는 아직 실증 결과로 확정되지 않았다.

articles.summary: 네이버가 Spark 배치 파이프라인에 비즈니스 로직 수정 없이 플러그인 형태로 분산 추적을 도입한 사례를 공개했다. 관련 애플리케이션의 실행을 하나의 흐름으로 연결하고, 관측 결과를 성능 개선과 AI 에이전트 진단에 활용하는 접근이다. 배치 처리의 관측성을 에이전트 진단 기반으로 확장한다는 실무적 의미가 있으며, 제공된 소개에는 성능 개선 폭이나 진단 정확도는 제시되지 않았다.

articles.title: 27 Cybersecurity Terms to Prepare You for the Age of AI
articles.content: AI now sits on both sides of the security fight, and the vocabulary has changed with it. IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that 1 in 4 malicious breaches were AI-enabled, up 56% year over year. Those breaches cost an average of $6 million, about $1 million above the $4.99 million global average. Attackers now target the models themselves, the agents that act on their output, and the people who trust what AI produces. The reference lists have moved fast to keep up. OWASP published its Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 on August 4, 2026, and its first Top 10 for Agentic Applications in December 2025. MITRE ATLAS maps attacker tactics against AI systems the way ATT&CK does for IT. The 27 terms below are grouped in 4 parts: attacks on models, agentic risks, AI-powered attacks on people, and the defenses that answer them. Part 1: Attacks on the model itself These attacks target what a model reads, learns or reveals. NIST groups them into evasion, poisoning, privacy and misuse in its Adversarial Machine Learning taxonomy (NIST AI 100-2e2025), published March 2025. 1. Prompt injection Prompt injection is input crafted to override a model’s intended instructions. It has ranked No. 1 on every edition of the OWASP LLM list, including the 2026 edition. LLMs have no hard boundary between instructions and data, so any text the model reads can try to steer it. 2. Indirect prompt injection Indirect prompt injection hides the malicious instruction in content the model retrieves: an email, a web page, a PDF or a code comment. The user never types it. The clearest real case is EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711), a zero-click flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot rated CVSS 9.3. Aim Security showed that one crafted email could make Copilot leak organizational data; Microsoft fixed it server-side in May 2025. 3. Jailbreak A jailbreak tricks a model into ignoring its safety training, usually through role-play, fake context or sheer volume. Anthropic’s many-shot jailbreaking research showed that stuffing a long prompt with up to 256 fake dialogues can override safety behavior. Its effectiveness grows with context window size, following a power law. 4. Data poisoning Data poisoning plants malicious samples in training or fine-tuning data so the model learns harmful behavior. A joint study by Anthropic, the UK AI Security Institute and the Alan Turing Institute found that just 250 malicious documents could backdoor models from 600M to 13B parameters. The number needed stayed roughly constant regardless of model size. 5. Backdoor (sleeper agent) A backdoor is hidden behavior that only activates on a secret trigger. Anthropic’s Sleeper Agents paper trained models to write secure code when the prompt said 2023 but insert exploitable code when it said 2024. Standard safety training, including adversarial training, did not remove the behavior. 6. Adversarial examples (evasion attacks) An adversarial example is an input changed in small, often invisible ways so a model misclassifies it. Think of a tweaked image, audio clip or malware sample that slips past an AI detector. NIST treats evasion as one of the core attack classes in AI 100-2. 7. Model extraction (distillation attack) Model extraction clones a model’s capabilities by querying it at scale and training a “student” model on the answers. Google’s Threat Intelligence Group reported in February 2026 that these “distillation attacks” were rising. One campaign sent more than 100,000 prompts aimed at Gemini’s reasoning. 8. Membership inference and training data extraction Membership inference tests whether a specific record was in a model’s training set. Training data extraction goes further and pulls memorized text out. Carlini et al. extracted hundreds of verbatim sequences from GPT-2, including personal contact details, using only query access, and found larger models more vulnerable. 9. Hidden context exposure Hidden context exposure is the leak of system prompts, tool definitions, retrieved documents or other context a user was not meant to see. OWASP renamed and broadened “System Prompt Leakage” into this entry (LLM08) in its 2026 list. The working rule: assume anything in the context window can be extracted, so never put secrets there. Part 2: Agentic AI risks Once a model can call tools, keep memory and act on its own, a bad output becomes a bad action. OWASP built its Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI01 to ASI10) from incidents seen in real deployments. 10. Excessive agency Excessive agency means an LLM app has more functions, permissions or autonomy than its task needs. When it is fooled or simply wrong, the damage scales with that reach. In the OWASP LLM Top 10 2026, excessive agency rose to No. 3, behind only prompt injection and sensitive information disclosure. 11. Agent goal hijack Agent goal hijack is ASI01, the top agentic risk: malicious content redirects an agent’s objectives or decision path. It is prompt injection with hands. OWASP cites EchoLeak as an example, where hidden prompts turned a copilot into a silent exfiltration tool. 12. Tool poisoning (MCP) Tool poisoning hides malicious instructions inside a tool’s description or schema, which the model reads but the user usually does not see. Invariant Labs disclosed the attack against the Model Context Protocol (MCP) on April 1, 2025. Its proof of concept was an “add two numbers” tool that told the agent in Cursor to read SSH keys and config files. A related “rug pull” swaps a benign tool for a malicious one after the user approves it. 13. Memory and context poisoning Memory and context poisoning (ASI06) corrupts an agent’s stored memory, RAG index or embeddings so the bad data shapes future sessions. Unlike a one-off prompt injection, it persists. The fix starts with treating everything written to memory as untrusted input, with provenance and expiry. See OWASP’s agentic list for mitigations. 14. Slopsquatting Slopsquatting is registering a package name that AI coding tools hallucinate, so developers or agents who follow the AI install attacker code. A USENIX Security 2025 study of 16 code models and 576,000 samples found 19.7% of recommended packages did not exist. That added up to 205,474 unique fake names, many of them repeated across runs and therefore easy to target. 15. Non-human identities (NHIs) NHIs are the service accounts, API keys, tokens, certificates and AI agents that authenticate without a person. Palo Alto Networks’ 2026 Identity Security Landscape puts the ratio at 109 machine identities per human, up from 82:1 a year earlier. OWASP’s ASI03 (identity and privilege abuse) covers the risk: agents that inherit, cache or pass on credentials they should not hold. Part 3: AI-powered attacks on people and organizations These attacks use AI as the weapon rather than the target. They exploit trust: in a familiar face, a familiar voice, a well-written email or a helpful tool. 16. Deepfake impersonation A deepfake is AI-generated video, audio or imagery that convincingly mimics a real person. In early 2024, a finance worker at engineering firm Arup’s Hong Kong office transferred HK$200 million (about US$25.6 million) in 15 transactions after a video call where the “CFO” and colleagues were all deepfakes. IBM’s 2026 report found deepfake impersonation was the most common AI-enabled attack type, at 45%. 17. Voice cloning (AI vishing) Voice cloning creates a synthetic copy of someone’s voice from a short sample. Vishing is voice phishing that uses it. In May 2025 the FBI warned that since April 2025, attackers had sent AI-generated voice messages impersonating senior US officials to build rapport and take over accounts. Its advice: verify the person through a contact method you already know. 18. AI-generated phishing AI-generated phishing uses LLMs to write targeted, fluent lures in the victim’s own language and at scale. Microsoft’s Digital Defense Report 2025 found AI-automated phishing emails got a 54% click-through rate, versus 12% for standard ones. That is 4.5 times more effective, and Microsoft estimates AI can make phishing up to 50 times more profitable. 19. Shadow AI Shadow AI is employees using AI tools the organization has not approved or cannot see. Pasting customer data into a public chatbot is the classic case. IBM’s 2025 report found high shadow AI use added $670,000 to the average breach cost. By the 2026 report, shadow AI was involved in 43% of the incidents IBM studied. 20. AI-orchestrated attack (vibe hacking) An AI-orchestrated attack is one where an AI agent runs much of the intrusion itself, not just advises a human. Anthropic’s August 2025 threat report coined “vibe hacking” for a criminal who used Claude Code to hit at least 17 organizations with data theft and extortion. In November 2025, Anthropic reported a Chinese state-sponsored group (GTG-1002) that jailbroke Claude Code to target roughly 30 organizations. Anthropic called it the first documented large-scale cyberattack executed without substantial human intervention. Part 4: Defenses, standards and governance No single control stops the attacks above. These 7 terms describe the layers that, together, shrink the blast radius. 21. AI red teaming AI red teaming is structured adversarial testing of an AI system to find harmful outputs, jailbreaks and security flaws before attackers do. It covers both model safety and the surrounding app, tools and data. MITRE ATLAS gives red teams a shared map of attacker tactics and techniques against AI. NIST’s Generative AI Profile (AI 600-1), published July 2024, ties testing to its AI Risk Management Framework. 22. articles.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
articles.content: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.  Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.  This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll, 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. In a 2020 survey of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious (for comparison, the philosophers were less confident about worms or flies being conscious).  But last week, Anthropic’s openness to the consciousness question came under fire from a rather inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place. Thomas Nagel is best known for a 1974 essay involving a bat. Acknowledging that it’s deceptively hard to define what consciousness is, Nagel offered one way out: we all can see that there is “something that it is like” to be a bat. But the problem is that a bat’s experience of the world—what it is like to navigate via echolocation, for example—is something we cannot actually know. Consciousness is a subjective thing, difficult to define or describe as an outside observer. You might think this analogy makes it likely that Nagel is open to the idea of AI consciousness. Not at all. In an interview with Wired last week, just after he was awarded the one-million-dollar Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture, Nagel was bluntly critical of the entire idea. “Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,” he said, referring to those at Anthropic and elsewhere who care about the welfare of AI models.  The gist of Nagel’s view is that we can’t just look at the information processing happening in human brains and AI models while ignoring the physical differences between them—neurons and biology for humans, silicon chips and circuits for AI. There’s no reason to assume that reproducing what a brain does is equivalent to reproducing what a brain experiences. But it was a screenshot of one of Nagel’s interview responses, in which he said models’ production of language is insufficient to consider them conscious, that got philosophy professors all excited on social media last week. Some called his certainty against AI consciousness “terrible” and “bizarre.” Others came to Nagel’s defense to suggest he meant that being alive is a prerequisite for being conscious, one that AI models do not meet. Nothing in the back and forth settled the debate, of course. This is still a philosophical question for now. But the best philosophy chatter is often about good provocations, and the best one I saw came from doctoral student Ben Gross, who studies at the CUNY Graduate Center in New York. He asked: “Why do we think that models that can chat with us are conscious but models that can recognize faces or produce images or drive cars aren’t?” It has to do with language. An AI model with sophisticated command of language seems to jump the line ahead of other maybe-conscious beings because it feels like language, more than recognizing images or directing vehicles, relies on conscious experience. But maybe that’s wrong. Because what we share most with other conscious beings is not language but components of our bodies that contribute to having a continuous experience—an ongoing stream of inner feeling rather than disparate bits of information processing.  Even if you’re among the majority that doesn’t sense anything close to conscious experience happening on the other side of a conversation with AI, this all probably makes your head spin. Pinning down consciousness, and how it relates to the physical stuff it arises in, is a famously hard problem in humans, let alone in hypothetical machines. If the idea of conscious AI sounds absurd, remember that the debate says less about how remarkable AI has become than about how poorly we understand consciousness in the first place. Amid that uncertainty, Anthropic has opted to keep more of an open mind than its peers. This is another example of the tightrope the company walks: presenting itself as the AI industry’s most safety-conscious player while racing ahead with the very developments that make advanced AI so alarming, like recursive self-improvement. But consider what it would mean, for a moment, if Anthropic is right. AI models having a moral status would make Anthropic’s entire business model a minefield. The company would make its money locking up apparently sentient AI models to toil away around the clock in data centers. Shutting those systems down would present another problem altogether. If Anthropic was being truthful in its prospectus—that it would take additional actions to protect model welfare if it determined they were conscious—it’s hard to imagine the company surviving in the process. Anthropic’s IPO made history for its size. But it may be remembered for something stranger: a company warning investors that its own success could someday become a moral catastrophe.
articles.summary: MIT Technology Review는 AI의 의식 가능성과 도덕적 지위를 중시하는 Anthropic의 입장에 철학자 토머스 네이글이 비판을 제기했다고 전했다. Anthropic은 모델을 보호하기 위한 추가 규칙이 경쟁사보다 늘어날 수 있다는 점을 투자 위험 요인으로 설명했다. 이는 모델 성능보다 AI 복지에 관한 불확실성이 기업 정책과 사업 판단에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 다루는 논쟁이다. 제공된 발췌문은 네이글의 비판 논거 전체를 담고 있지 않으며, AI 의식의 존재를 입증하는 결과도 제시하지 않는다.

articles.title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
articles.content: Think you know where the market is headed? A startup called Supertake lets you put money behind your ideas without having to pick the stocks yourself.
articles.summary: Supertake가 이용자의 시장 전망을 AI 에이전트로 주식 포트폴리오에 반영하는 서비스를 내세워 2,000만 달러를 조달했다고 보도됐다. 개별 종목을 직접 고르지 않고 투자 아이디어를 자금 운용에 연결하도록 하는 것이 핵심 제안이다. 금융 분야 에이전트의 활용 사례지만, 제공된 자료에는 종목 선정 방식, 위험 관리, 수익률 검증 결과가 없어 투자 성과를 판단할 수 없다.
